selected_text: Hypothesis: decoding every named and numeric HTML character reference for the URI policy comparison will remove entity-hidden disallowed schemes, because the serializer keeps the original reference spelling while the policy sees the resolved scheme. Prerequisite: a policy-local decoder built from the parser's named-entity table plus decimal and hexadecimal numeric parsing. Bounded test: sanitize link attributes containing hex, decimal, uppercase-hex, named-colon, named-tab, named-newline and numeric-control variants of javascript: and file:, then compare against allowed http(s), mailto, relative, query-ampersand and custom-protocol controls. Expected result: all entity-hidden disallowed values lose the URI attribute; allowed and relative values keep their exact serialized bytes. Falsifier: any entity-hidden scheme survives, or any allowed control changes bytes. Cleanup: revert the one policy line and helper in the disposable copy; limitations: the comparison value is decoded but the emitted value intentionally stays encoded.
